subject: math

objective.text: Measure and record data in a table. Answer questions about the data and tell what it shows.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective

explanations.title: Measure your handspan
explanations.text: Your handspan is the length from your pinky tip to your thumb tip. Stretch your fingers out. Start measuring at zero on the ruler. Say about how many inches it is.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 1

explanations.title: Record data with tally marks
explanations.text: Each person gets one tally mark in the row for their handspan. Count the tally marks in a row to know how many people have that handspan.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 1

explanations.title: Most common and least common
explanations.text: The most common handspan has the most tally marks. The least common handspan has the fewest tally marks.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 1 and 2

explanations.title: Ask a comparison question
explanations.text: A comparison question asks how many more. To answer it, subtract the smaller count from the bigger count. Use the numbers in the table.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 2; Student Debrief

explanations.title: 100 more than
explanations.text: 300 minus 200 is 100. So 100 more than 200 is 300. Say the subtraction as a how many more sentence.

source_ref.section: Fluency: How Many More Hundreds

examples.title: Comparing handspans
examples.text: Suppose 7 people have a handspan of 5 inches and 2 people have 8 inches. 7 minus 2 equals 5. 5 more people have a handspan of 5 inches than 8 inches.

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.
Diffusion is allowed only for: style or background art, and single icons (one ball, one pencil, one leaf, one character) that code then tiles to the exact count.
Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
Visual explanations are valid only when the asset exists (pipeline doc, Planner rules).
